slides.say: In the accompanying figure, a is parallel to b. What is the value of x?
This time the line between a and b bends twice. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with the zig-zag rule, and then with a parallel line through each bend.

[short pause] First by understanding, with the zig-zag rule. The angles whose tips point left add up to the angles whose tips point right. Forty points left, and sixty-five points left. x points right, and thirty-five points right.

So forty plus sixty-five equals x plus thirty-five. Forty plus sixty-five is a hundred five. x plus thirty-five is a hundred five, so x is a hundred five minus thirty-five, which is seventy. Choice number two is our answer.
at: so x is a hundred five minus
Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Careful, a hundred five, choice number three, adds only the left side. And a hundred forty, choice number four, adds everything.

[pause] Now the math way. Not sure you remember the rule? Draw a parallel line through each bend. That always works. Start at the bottom, at the lower bend, the sixty-five, and draw one more line through it, parallel to a and b.
The new line splits the sixty-five in two. The lower part makes a Z with the thirty-five at line b, so it's thirty-five. The upper part is sixty-five minus thirty-five, which is thirty.
at: The lower part makes a Z

slides.say: Now the upper bend, the x. Draw a parallel line through it too. It splits x in two. The lower part of x makes a Z with that thirty, so it's thirty. The upper part of x makes the Z with the forty at line a, so it's forty.
at: Draw a parallel line through it too

slides.say: So x is forty plus thirty, which is seventy. Choice number two again. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: So x is forty plus thirty
